Right, so—no food in the house, Bram's about to blow five sim getting to the outcrop, and I'm standing here with twelve hundred and no plan. Characteristic start.

Let me get my bearings first—see what's actually here with me, and what I'd need to spend just to get to farmland for work. Because the math's already looking thin if I'm burning five there and five back and nobody's eaten yet. So the farmland's ten sim-roundtrip before I've lifted a finger, and I haven't seen whether Bram's actually going yet or if he's still standing here chewing on empty pockets. Right, so—let me work this out loud, get Bram's attention, maybe shake something loose. Because Perrin's right: no food, no cushion, and burning sim on travel when we haven't even looked at what a day's harvest pays?

Actually, hold on. Before I say anything—let me check what I've actually got in my hands, what I started with. Because if there's something tradeable, something I can turn into food or faster work, I need to know now.  Five sim to harvest, minimum, and I'm standing here empty-handed. No food, no tools of my own, and if I'm bragging about forestry work to Corwin while I'm still just a day laborer hopping fields—right, so I need to actually get there first, don't I? Let me check what a trip to the farmland actually costs, because Perrin's right. Ten sim there and back is twenty gone before I've earned, and that's if I don't starve first.

But actually—hold on. Nell said "the marker can wait" and sent Bram to the outcrop, Ainsley and Perrin to sort food. So someone's got to handle food, and if I'm standing here anyway, I could—no, I could go with Bram. No, that's stupid, the outcrop's for miners.

Right, so—let me just say something. Bram's still here, Perrin's still here, and we're all burning daylight while nobody's eaten. I'll jump into this conversation, try to shake something loose. Because if Bram's going to the outcrop and I'm going to farmland, we're both burning sim on travel, and nobody's asked where the food's coming from yet.  Bram's already gone—right, so he didn't wait. Perrin's here, at least. So Bram's burning five sim getting to the outcrop, and me and Perrin are still standing here with empty pockets and empty stomachs. 

Right, so—I'm chasing work, but I need to eat before I work, or I'll be burning more sim just healing myself, won't I? Let's think about this. I could go to farmland—five sim there, five back, harvest costs five minimum. That's fifteen sim to earn... what? I don't even know what a crop pays. Or I could find someone with food and try to trade, but I've got nothing in my hands to trade.

Unless—right, so Perrin's here. Did Ainsley actually leave with a plan, or is everyone else just scattering? Let me see who's still actually in this house with me. Because if Nell's at carpentry, Bram's walking to outcrop, and Ainsley's... somewhere, then it's just me and Perrin figuring out how we eat today.

Actually, wait. Before I say anything else—I need to know what work actually pays. What does harvesting even earn me? Because if I'm going to spend fifteen sim to get there and work, I need to know if that's worth more than just... doing something else. Let me find out what the farmland situation actually is.  Empty. Right, so I'd be working alone, which is fine—I'm used to that. But I've still got the travel cost problem. Let me think about this differently. I need food, I need work, and I need to not burn all my sim just getting between places.

What if I look at who's actually selling food? Marta's the baker, right? She runs business:b_bakery. Maybe I go there, buy something cheap to fill myself, then head to work. Or—actually, even better—maybe I can find work AT the bakery, or near it. Because right now I'm burning sim on speculation, and I can't afford speculation.

But hold on. Let me check what travel to the farmland actually costs me specifically, since I need real numbers, not guesses.   One sim. That's—right, so that's just the flat minimum, which means farmland's basically next door. Perrin was wrong about the five, or that was just Bram's outcrop distance. So I'm looking at one sim to get there, one back, five to harvest. Seven sim total to earn... whatever a crop is worth.

That's not terrible. I could do that. But I'm still hungry now, and if I go work hungry, I might end up costing myself more in the long run. Unless—what if I can harvest something I can eat raw? Some crops you can eat right off the plant, can't you?

Right, so I need to know what crops are actually growing. Are there specific farmland plots, specific crops? Because if I can harvest something edible and just eat it without cooking, that solves my immediate problem. Let me check what farmland options I've actually got.  Right, so—cabbage, carrots, corn, potatoes, tomatoes. Those I can eat. Barley, wheat, cotton, soybeans—those need processing. Rice needs milling, doesn't it? Or cooking at least.

So my best bet is head to one of the vegetable plots, harvest something raw I can eat immediately, then I'm fueled for more work. Potato's probably the most filling. Carrot's quick energy. Tomato's... well, it's food.

But here's the thing—I don't know which of these plots is actually stocked with crops ready to harvest. What if I walk to farmland:potato and there's nothing there? Then I've burned sim for nothing.

Right, so I should—actually, maybe I should talk to Wren Thorne first? He's the farmer, he knows what's growing where. He'd know which plots are actually producing. But that's more travel, more sim burned on uncertainty.

Or I just pick one and hope. Carrots grow fast, don't they? And they're ready early. Potatoes take longer but give more. Tomatoes need warmth...

Let me check what the actual cost would be to get to a specific plot, then to harvest. Because if I'm going to gamble, I want to know the exact stake.  And harvest cost?

One to get there, five to harvest. That's six total. I get one potato, I eat it for free, I'm up one food and I've spent six sim. Then I can work the rest of the day with actual energy.

But wait—I should check if Perrin's got any better ideas, or if Ainsley's out there actually finding food like Nell said. Because if someone's buying food for the house, I don't need to solve this alone.

Actually, right—Perrin's still here. Let me ask them what they know before I go charging off. Because Perrin's a student, they might know something about... I don't know, market prices? What food actually costs?   Right, so they're hearing me now. Perrin's got to have some sense of the numbers—they're studying, they've got to know something about how this town actually runs. I need to know if I'm being stupid rushing off to farm, or if that's actually my best play.

Because I'm standing here burning daylight while Bram's already earning at the outcrop, and if Perrin's got a better lead—or if Ainsley actually bought food and we're waiting for nothing—then I'm wasting my morning.

Actually, you know what, while I'm waiting for Perrin to answer, let me think ahead. If Perrin doesn't know anything useful, I'm going to farmland. One sim to get to potato patch, five to harvest one potato. Eat it immediately—that's zero cost. Then I'd have one food in me and eleven ninety-three left. Then I'd need to know—can I harvest more and sell them? Or should I just work all day at the patch, harvest as much as I can, then sell the surplus?

But I don't know who buys potatoes. Ainsley's a trader, but they're off sorting food, not necessarily buying crops. Marta the baker might mill them into flour? I don't even know if that's a thing you can do with potatoes.

Right, so if I don't know the market, I'm gambling. But staying here and starving is also gambling. At least farming gives me food I can eat if I can't sell it.

Wait—actually, I should check if there's anyone at the farmland right now. Because if I'm going to work alone, fine. But if there's already someone there, maybe I can learn something, or find out prices, or just not be the only one figuring this out.

But no, I checked earlier—empty. So it's just me.

Perrin, c'mon. Say something useful.

Right, so—I'm alone now. Perrin's off to college walking hungry, Bram's gone to the mine, and I'm standing here with twelve hundred minus three—no, I already spent three on that last thing I said, didn't I? Wait, no, that was just thinking. But I said something already, spent the three sim. So I'm at eleven ninety-seven sim.

And Perrin walked to college. That's—right, so college is four sim from here. They're burning four sim, arriving hungry, hoping to learn something while they're starving. Characteristic Holloway move, really. We all do it.

But me? I'm still here at the quarry house with empty hands and a rumbling gut, and my work is supposedly at farmland, but I'm starting to think "day laborer" means "go where someone's already working and hope they pay you," not "show up at an empty field and wait for crops to grow."

Right, so here's my actual options now:

One: Walk to farmland and harvest something I can eat raw—potato, carrot, tomato. Six sim total return trip, five to harvest, one to eat. Net expense: eleven sim for one food. Then I'm fed, but I've burned eleven sim and I'm still at square one for earning.

Two: Walk to farmland, harvest MORE than I eat—harvest five potatoes, eat one, sell four. But sell to WHO? Ainsley's the trader, but they're off "sorting food" and probably don't have a stall running yet. Marta's the baker, but she's at her bakery. Corwin's the forester. I don't actually know who buys crops.

Three: Forget farming, find actual work. Go to where someone's working and ask if they need hands. Bram's at the outcrop—he's mining, that's skilled. Forestry with Corwin or Idris—trade I asked about, didn't get, still want. Carpentry with Nell—skilled, probably no use for day labor.

Four: Find Wren Thorne, the actual farmer. He knows what's growing, what's ready, who's buying. If anyone's hiring day labor, Wren would know.

But I don't know where Wren IS right now. Could be at farmland, could be at home, could be anywhere.

Right, so—here's what I know for certain. I'm burning three sim per line I speak. I just spoke. Bram's gone, Perrin's gone, Nell's gone. I'm alone in a house that has no food.

The smart move is stop talking to myself and DO something. Either go to farmland and gamble on harvesting, or go find Wren, or find whoever's actually hiring TODAY.

But wait—can I even work at farmland if it's empty? "Your work is at Kasukabe Farmland" just means that's my supposed workplace, doesn't mean there's work there. Harvesting costs sim regardless of whether anyone's paying me to do it.

Right, so I need to find OUT. Find Wren, ask about work. Or just show up at farmland and see if anyone's there now that some time's passed.

Actually—you know what, let me check this first. I've been assuming farmland is empty because I checked earlier. But that was ticks ago. Perrin's walked to college, Bram's walked to mine—maybe Wren walked to farm. Let me look again before I commit to anything.

But I already know what that costs. One sim just to look. Then another to move if I decide to go.

Right, so—screw it. I'm going to farmland. It's one sim, I'll see what's there. If Wren's there, I ask for work. If it's empty, I harvest a potato, eat it, and figure out the rest of the day from there.

That's the plan. Stop talking, start moving. </think>  Right, so—I'm here. One sim spent, eleven ninety-six remaining. Now what do I actually see?

Let me look around. Is anyone here—Wren, or anyone else working? What's growing that's ready to harvest? What's my actual move now that I've burned the travel cost? </think>  Still empty. Right, so Wren's not here, nobody's here. I'm alone in a field with twelve crop patches named and me burning daylight.

But look—cabbage, carrot, corn, cotton, potato, rice, soybean, tomato, wheat, barley. That's ten specific plots I can walk to. And I can eat cabbage, carrot, corn, potato, tomato raw. Rice needs milling. Cotton's not food. Soybean might need cooking. Wheat and barley definitely need processing.

So my play is: pick one, harvest, eat, decide if I stay or go.

Potato's the most filling, right? Carb-heavy, keeps you going. Carrot's quick energy but lighter. Tomato's... vitamins, I guess. Cabbage is bulky but not dense. Corn's good but might need cooking? No, fresh corn you can eat raw.

Right, so potato's my bet. Most calories per unit. If I harvest one potato, eat it, I'm fueled for more work. Costs five sim to harvest, one to move here already spent. Six total, I'm at eleven ninety.

But then what? If I just leave, I'm down six sim with nothing to show. If I harvest more and try to sell... who's buying? Marta's the baker—she might buy wheat or barley, not potatoes. Ainsley's the trader—might buy anything, but where are they?

Actually, wait. The list shows "business:b_bakery" as a place I could go. Marta's there. I could go there after harvesting, try to sell surplus. But that's more travel, more sim burned.

Right, so better plan: harvest enough that I'm confident I can eat AND sell. Harvest three potatoes—fifteen sim, eat one (free), sell two. If they sell for three each, I'm up six minus sixteen travel and harvest... no, that math's terrible. I'd be down ten sim for two food I didn't eat.

Unless... potatoes sell for more than I think. I don't know prices. This is the problem with being a day laborer—I'm always working blind.

Right, so here's what I do. I harvest ONE potato right now. Eleven ninety-six minus five is eleven ninety-one. I eat it immediately. Now I have food in me, I'm not risking health. Then I decide: stay and harvest more for sale, or move on to find actual paid work.

If I stay and harvest, I'm gambling on finding a buyer. If I move, I'm gambling on finding someone hiring. Both are gambles. But at least fed, I can work longer.

Potato patch. That's where I'm going. One sim to move there, then harvest. Then eat. Then reassess.  </think>   Arrived at potato patch. Another sim spent, eleven ninety-five remaining. Ten ninety-five sim remaining, one food consumed. Now I've got a baseline. I'm not hungry anymore, which means I can think about earning instead of just surviving.

But here's the thing: I'm standing in a potato patch with no buyers in sight. I could harvest more, try to find Ainsley or Marta, see if they'll buy. Or I could cut my losses—I'm already down six sim in travel and harvest—and find actual paid work.

Wait, actually. Let me think about who might actually want potatoes. Marta's a baker. Bakers don't bake potatoes, they bake bread. But maybe she buys them to sell raw? Or maybe there's a market stall somewhere.

Or—and this is the thought I keep having—what if I just keep harvesting and stockpile? If nobody's buying today, maybe someone buys tomorrow. But that's sim tied up in inventory, sim I'm not earning interest on, and I need regular income.

Right, so I'm torn between two bad options: harvest more here and hope for a buyer, or leave and look for guaranteed work. But "guaranteed" work is a joke—I'm a day laborer, nothing's guaranteed.

Actually, check this: I could go to business:b_bakery right now. It's in the list of places I can go from here. Marta's there. If she's buying anything, I can try to sell her potatoes. If she's not, maybe she's got bread for sale—expensive, but if I'm desperate for food tomorrow, it's an option.

Or I could find Wren Thorne. The actual farmer. He'd know who's buying crops, what the market looks like. But I don't know where Wren is.

Right, so here's my play: harvest two more potatoes. That's ten sim, brings me to ten eighty-five. Then I've got three potatoes total—one eaten, two to sell. I carry them to the bakery, try to sell to Marta. If she buys, great. If not, I eat another and try elsewhere.

But wait—can I even carry three potatoes? I don't know my inventory limit. What if I harvest two more and I'm overweight? Then I'm stuck.

Screw it. I'm cautious now. Let me just go to the bakery with what I've got—one potato to potentially sell, and ten ninety-five sim. If Marta's buying, great. If not, I'm only down travel costs and I can reassess.

Two sim to get to bakery from here, right? Let me check actual cost before I commit.   Actually, let me just go. I'm burning daylight standing here talking to myself. Marta might be my only shot at a buyer today. If she's not buying potatoes, maybe she needs labor—sweeping floors, carrying flour, whatever. Desperate day's desperate measures, right?

But before I go—should I harvest one more, just in case? Have something to actually sell, not just... myself?

No, no. That's four more sim on a gamble. I'm already committed. Go to bakery, talk to Marta, find out what the market actually is. That's information worth paying travel for. Information about work, about prices, about who's hiring.

Right, so—I'm moving to business:b_bakery. Two sim? Three? Whatever it costs. Let's find out.   I'm actually not sure what costs what. But standing here isn't earning me anything or teaching me anything. I need to talk to Marta. So I'm going to the bakery. Moving to business:b_bakery.   Two more sim spent, ten ninety-three remaining. I'm at the bakery. Let me see who's actually here, and if Marta's working or just... baking without customers.   I'm at the bakery door, or inside? Let me look around. Figure out if I'm talking to Marta Thorne or just standing in empty space.  Right, so I'm here now—two sim spent getting from potato patch to bakery. Ten ninety-three in hand. Let me see what I'm actually looking at. Is Marta here? Anyone buying or selling? What's the lay of the land?
